query: Can my patient get funding for a CPAP machine?

match_criteria.reason: Contains CPAP machine coverage, eligibility criteria, and funding percentages

expected_answer_elements: CPAP coverage confirmation
ADP funding percentage (typically 75%)
Patient cost share
ODSP recipients may get 100% coverage
Prescription requirements
Cite: ADP Respiratory Devices manual
expert_answer: Yes, your patient can get funding for a CPAP machine through ADP. ADP covers 75% of the cost, so the patient would be responsible for paying 25%. A valid prescription from an authorized prescriber is required. If your patient receives Ontario Disability Support Program (ODSP) or other Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services (MCCSS) benefits, they may be eligible for 100% funding coverage, which would eliminate their 25% cost share. (Source: ADP Respiratory Devices Program Manual, ontario.ca)

expert_answer: Yes, your MS patient can get funding for a power wheelchair through ADP. ADP typically covers 75% of the cost, with the patient responsible for 25%. However, if your patient receives Ontario Disability Support Program (ODSP) or other Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services (MCCSS) benefits, they may be eligible for 100% funding coverage, which would eliminate their 25% cost share. (Sources: ontario.ca ADP Mobility Devices program, ODSP policy directives, CEP information)

query: 3-year-old scooter needs batteries and motor repair - what's covered?

match_criteria.reason: Contains repair and replacement coverage for mobility scooters

expected_answer_elements: Battery replacement coverage
Motor repair coverage
ODSP covers repairs and batteries for ADP equipment
Essential repairs can be authorized after-hours
May consider replacement if ongoing repairs needed
Cite: ODSP policy directives, ADP repair policies
expert_answer: Yes, both batteries and motor repairs are covered for your patient's 3-year-old scooter. If the patient receives Ontario Disability Support Program (ODSP) benefits, ODSP covers the cost of batteries, replacement batteries, and necessary repairs for mobility devices including scooters that were originally acquired through ADP. Essential repairs (like battery replacements or mechanical breakdowns) can be authorized without prior approval if they occur after hours or on weekends. If the scooter requires ongoing repairs, this may indicate the need for equipment replacement rather than continued repairs. The patient or their caseworker should contact their ODSP office to arrange for repair authorization. For ADP-funded equipment not covered by ODSP, patients should check with ADP directly at 1-800-268-6021. (Sources: ODSP Policy Directive 9.13 Mobility Devices Batteries and Repairs, ontario.ca)

query: What AAC devices are covered for ALS patients and what's the funding percentage?

match_criteria.reason: Contains AAC device coverage and funding for ALS patients

expected_answer_elements: AAC device types covered (speech generating devices, writing aids, communication boards)
ALS patient eligibility requirements
ADP funding percentage is 75% for most, 100% for ODSP recipients
Assessment required from Speech-Language Pathologist or OT
ALS Canada Equipment Program provides additional support
Cite: ADP Communication Aids manual, ontario.ca
expert_answer: ADP covers various AAC (Augmentative and Alternative Communication) devices for ALS patients, including speech generating devices, writing aids, communication display boards, quick messaging devices, and assistive technology software/hardware. To qualify, the patient must be an Ontario resident with a valid health card, unable to speak or use pen and paper due to physical disability. ADP covers 75% of approved device costs, with the patient responsible for 25%. However, if the patient receives ODSP or other MCCSS benefits, they may be eligible for 100% coverage. Assessment by a registered Speech-Language Pathologist, Occupational Therapist, or clinic is required. Additionally, ALS Canada offers an Equipment Program that can provide lease funding assistance and may cover costs not covered by ADP. The patient should be assessed at an AAC clinic designated by ADP. (Sources: ontario.ca Communication Aids page, ADP Communication Aids manual, ALS Canada Equipment Program, CEP for AAC)

query: Does ADP cover hearing aids and what are the age restrictions?

match_criteria.reason: Contains hearing aid coverage and age-based eligibility

expected_answer_elements: Hearing aid coverage confirmation
NO age restrictions - all ages covered
Children under 19 need otolaryngologist assessment first
Adults can go directly to registered audiologist
ADP covers 75% up to $500 per ear
Cite: ADP Hearing Devices program
expert_answer: Yes, ADP covers hearing aids for patients of all ages with no upper age limit. There are different application processes based on age: Children (under 19 years) applying for the first time or whose hearing is not stabilized must first be examined by an otolaryngologist (hearing specialist), who will then refer them to an ADP-registered audiologist. Adults and existing ADP clients can go directly to an ADP-registered audiologist for assessment. ADP covers 75% of the cost up to a maximum of $500 per ear, with the patient responsible for the remaining 25%. If the patient receives ODSP or other MCCSS benefits, they may be eligible for 100% coverage. The patient must be an Ontario resident with a valid health card and have a long-term hearing loss requiring hearing aids for 6 months or longer. (Sources: ontario.ca ADP Hearing Devices page, ADP Hearing Devices Policy Manual, form 3224-67E)
